units.description: Place a cause before another past event and keep agreement clear.

lessons.title: Before another past event
lessons.outcome: I can show that one past action happened before another.

targets.label: Before another past event
targets.explanation: Imperfetto of avere or essere plus a past participle places an event earlier than a past reference point. The later event commonly uses passato prossimo or imperfetto; the earlier one uses trapassato prossimo.

repair.title: Try before another past event again
repair.body: Imperfetto of avere or essere plus a past participle places an event earlier than a past reference point. The later event commonly uses passato prossimo or imperfetto; the earlier one uses trapassato prossimo.

examples.it: Quando sono arrivato, Anna era già partita.
examples.en: When I arrived, Anna had already left.

lessons.title: Earlier movement and agreement
lessons.outcome: I can place an earlier movement before a later event with essere.

targets.label: Earlier movement and agreement
targets.explanation: Use ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate or erano plus the past participle of a movement verb. With essere, the participle follows the subject: uscito, uscita, usciti, uscite.

repair.title: Try earlier movement and agreement again
repair.body: Use ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate or erano plus the past participle of a movement verb. With essere, the participle follows the subject: uscito, uscita, usciti, uscite.

examples.it: Quando ho chiamato, Giulia era già uscita.
examples.en: When I called, Giulia had already gone out.

lessons.title: Explain a prior cause
lessons.outcome: I can explain a past result with an action that had already happened.

targets.label: Explain a prior cause
targets.explanation: Name the state or event that needs an explanation. Use trapassato for the prior action that caused the result.

repair.title: Try explain a prior cause again
repair.body: Name the state or event that needs an explanation. Use trapassato for the prior action that caused the result.

examples.it: Non siamo entrati nel museo.
examples.en: We did not enter the museum.

units.title: Describe how life changed
units.description: Contrast old routines with a particular event and the present.

lessons.title: Repeated life in the past
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish an old routine from a single completed occasion.

targets.label: Repeated life in the past
targets.explanation: Use imperfetto with habitual markers such as ogni estate or da bambino. A dated or singled-out event normally takes passato prossimo in conversational narration.

repair.title: Try repeated life in the past again
repair.body: Use imperfetto with habitual markers such as ogni estate or da bambino. A dated or singled-out event normally takes passato prossimo in conversational narration.

examples.it: Da piccola andavo spesso al mare.
examples.en: As a child, I often went to the sea.

lessons.title: Compare then and now
lessons.outcome: I can compare a former routine with a present routine.

targets.label: Compare then and now
targets.explanation: Un tempo plus imperfetto presents a repeated old situation. Adesso plus the present makes the contrast easy to follow.

repair.title: Try compare then and now again
repair.body: Un tempo plus imperfetto presents a repeated old situation. Adesso plus the present makes the contrast easy to follow.

examples.it: Un tempo andavo al lavoro in autobus.
examples.en: I used to go to work by bus.

steps.title: Describe a change in daily life

lessons.title: A habit that ended
lessons.outcome: I can say how long a former situation lasted and when it changed.

targets.label: A habit that ended
targets.explanation: For a completed three-year period, use passato prossimo; reserve imperfetto for an old habit or background state. A completed move ends the old situation.

repair.title: Try a habit that ended again
repair.body: For a completed three-year period, use passato prossimo; reserve imperfetto for an old habit or background state. A completed move ends the old situation.

examples.it: Per tre anni ho abitato a Torino.
examples.en: For three years I lived in Turin.

units.title: Give and request things
units.description: Refer clearly to recipients and objects in messages and requests.

lessons.title: Keep the recipient clear
lessons.outcome: I can use a recipient pronoun without losing track of who receives something.

targets.label: Keep the recipient clear
targets.explanation: Introduce the person before replacing the name with a pronoun. Gli can refer to a male singular recipient; the context must identify him.

repair.title: Try keep the recipient clear again
repair.body: Introduce the person before replacing the name with a pronoun. Gli can refer to a male singular recipient; the context must identify him.

examples.it: Ho scritto a Sara. Le ho mandato la mail.
examples.en: I wrote to Sara. I sent her the email.

lessons.title: Give it to someone
lessons.outcome: I can combine an indirect object pronoun with a direct one.

targets.label: Give it to someone
targets.explanation: The indirect pronoun comes first: mi, ti, gli/le becomes me, te, glie- before lo, la, li, le. Gli and le both form glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele; context tells the recipient.

repair.title: Try give it to someone again

examples.it: Il libro? Te lo presto domani.
examples.en: The book? I’ll lend it to you tomorrow.

lessons.title: Ask someone to pass it on
lessons.outcome: I can use a combined pronoun in a request or answer.

targets.label: Ask someone to pass it on
targets.explanation: Me lo refers to an already known masculine object being sent or given to me. In a familiar affirmative command, the pair attaches: mandamelo. Keep the recipient and object clear.

repair.title: Try ask someone to pass it on again
repair.body: Me lo refers to an already known masculine object being sent or given to me. In a familiar affirmative command, the pair attaches: mandamelo. Keep the recipient and object clear.

examples.it: Il modulo? Me lo puoi mandare?
examples.en: The form? Can you send it to me?

steps.title: Get a document from a friend

units.title: Places and quantities
units.description: Replace a known place, item or amount without losing the referent.

lessons.title: Ci for a place
lessons.outcome: I can refer back to a known place with ci.

targets.label: Ci for a place
targets.explanation: Ci can stand for a place already mentioned, often with andare, essere or tornare. With a finite verb, ci normally goes immediately before it.

repair.title: Try ci for a place again
repair.body: Ci can stand for a place already mentioned, often with andare, essere or tornare. With a finite verb, ci normally goes immediately before it.

examples.it: Vai spesso a Roma? Sì, ci vado ogni mese.
examples.en: Do you go to Rome often? Yes, I go there every month.

lessons.title: Ne for some or of it
lessons.outcome: I can replace a previously named quantity or di phrase with ne.

targets.label: Ne for some or of it
targets.explanation: Ne means some of them or of it; keep the quantity word if it matters. Ne can replace di questo, di lui, di loro after verbs such as parlare.

repair.title: Try ne for some or of it again
repair.body: Ne means some of them or of it; keep the quantity word if it matters. Ne can replace di questo, di lui, di loro after verbs such as parlare.

examples.it: Quante mele vuoi? Ne prendo tre.
examples.en: How many apples do you want? I’ll take three.

lessons.title: Say how many are needed
lessons.outcome: I can respond to a quantity question using ce ne.

targets.label: Say how many are needed
targets.explanation: Ne means of the already named items; ci means to/for us in these servire/mancare examples and changes to ce before ne. Ce ne servono due means we need two of them; ce ne manca una means we are missing one of them. The needed/missing items are the grammatical subject, so the verb agrees with the quantity. With voglio, Ne voglio quattro means I want four of them: no ci is required.

repair.title: Try say how many are needed again
repair.body: Ne means of the already named items; ci means to/for us in these servire/mancare examples and changes to ce before ne. Ce ne servono due means we need two of them; ce ne manca una means we are missing one of them. The needed/missing items are the grammatical subject, so the verb agrees with the quantity. With voglio, Ne voglio quattro means I want four of them: no ci is required.

examples.it: Ce ne servono due. Ne voglio quattro.
examples.en: We need two of them. I want four of them.

units.title: Identify people and things
units.description: Use relative clauses and explicit reference to guide a listener.

lessons.title: Che and cui
lessons.outcome: I can link a noun to a clause using che or cui.

targets.label: Che and cui
targets.explanation: Che links a noun to a clause when the noun is subject or direct object there. Use cui for an indirect relationship such as a cui or di cui.

repair.title: Try che and cui again
repair.body: Che links a noun to a clause when the noun is subject or direct object there. Use cui for an indirect relationship such as a cui or di cui.

examples.it: La persona che parla è mia sorella.
examples.en: The person who is speaking is my sister.

lessons.title: The right preposition before cui
lessons.outcome: I can carry a verb’s required preposition into a relative clause.

targets.label: The right preposition before cui
targets.explanation: If you say parlare con Marco, say Marco con cui parlo. Use in cui for “in which/when” and a cui for “to whom/which.”

repair.title: Try the right preposition before cui again
repair.body: If you say parlare con Marco, say Marco con cui parlo. Use in cui for “in which/when” and a cui for “to whom/which.”

examples.it: La donna con cui lavoro è gentile.
examples.en: The woman I work with is kind.

lessons.title: Avoid an unclear reference
lessons.outcome: I can repeat a noun or choose a relative clause so listeners know whom I mean.

targets.label: Avoid an unclear reference
targets.explanation: In La collega che ha chiamato, the colleague is the caller. A repeated noun avoids an ambiguous lui or lei.

repair.title: Try avoid an unclear reference again
repair.body: In La collega che ha chiamato, the colleague is the caller. A repeated noun avoids an ambiguous lui or lei.

examples.it: La collega che ha chiamato ha lasciato un messaggio.
examples.en: The colleague who called left a message.

steps.title: Give clear directions to a person

units.title: Make a workable plan
units.description: State real conditions, alternatives and a revised arrangement.

lessons.title: If it happens
lessons.outcome: I can use se with an open, realistic condition.

targets.label: If it happens
targets.explanation: For a possible situation, se normally takes indicative present or future, depending on time. A future result may follow a present condition.

repair.title: Try if it happens again
repair.body: For a possible situation, se normally takes indicative present or future, depending on time. A future result may follow a present condition.

examples.it: Se piove, restiamo a casa.
examples.en: If it rains, we stay home.

lessons.title: Offer realistic alternatives
lessons.outcome: I can propose two workable options depending on what happens.

targets.label: Offer realistic alternatives
targets.explanation: A present form after se can refer to a real future possibility. Altrimenti tells the listener what will happen if the condition fails.

repair.title: Try offer realistic alternatives again
repair.body: A present form after se can refer to a real future possibility. Altrimenti tells the listener what will happen if the condition fails.

examples.it: Se sei libero sabato, andiamo al cinema.
examples.en: If you are free Saturday, we can go to the cinema.

lessons.title: Change a plan politely
lessons.outcome: I can explain a condition and suggest a practical replacement plan.

targets.label: Change a plan politely
targets.explanation: Explain the condition that might disrupt the arrangement. An alternative time lets the other person respond.

repair.title: Try change a plan politely again
repair.body: Explain the condition that might disrupt the arrangement. An alternative time lets the other person respond.

examples.it: Se il treno è in ritardo, non arrivo per le otto.
examples.en: If the train is late, I will not arrive by eight.

units.title: Explain a problem
units.description: Connect reasons, aims, consequences, obstacles and sequence.

lessons.title: Because or in order to
lessons.outcome: I can choose a reason or purpose clause according to meaning.

targets.label: Because or in order to
targets.explanation: Perché plus an indicative fact can give the reason for an action. Per plus infinitive expresses a purpose when the understood subject is the same.

repair.title: Try because or in order to again
repair.body: Perché plus an indicative fact can give the reason for an action. Per plus infinitive expresses a purpose when the understood subject is the same.

examples.it: Sono rimasto a casa perché pioveva.
examples.en: I stayed home because it was raining.

lessons.title: Result and surprise
lessons.outcome: I can link a result or a fact that contrasts with expectation.

targets.label: Result and surprise
targets.explanation: A high degree may be followed by così...che to show what happened as a result. Anche se introduces a real fact that did not stop the other event.

repair.title: Try result and surprise again
repair.body: A high degree may be followed by così...che to show what happened as a result. Anche se introduces a real fact that did not stop the other event.

examples.it: Era così stanco che si è addormentato.
examples.en: He was so tired that he fell asleep.

lessons.title: Before and after
lessons.outcome: I can sequence actions and choose infinitive or finite clauses.

targets.label: Before and after
targets.explanation: Use prima di plus infinitive when the same person does both actions. Use prima che plus subjunctive when the later event has its own subject. After a real completed event, dopo che commonly takes indicative.

repair.title: Try before and after again
repair.body: Use prima di plus infinitive when the same person does both actions. Use prima che plus subjunctive when the later event has its own subject. After a real completed event, dopo che commonly takes indicative.

examples.it: Prima di uscire, spengo le luci.
examples.en: Before going out, I switch off the lights.

steps.title: Give a short set of instructions

units.title: Hopes and doubts
units.description: Build and use a limited, explicitly introduced present subjunctive toolkit.

lessons.title: A limited present subjunctive toolkit
lessons.outcome: I can recognize and make frequent present subjunctive forms for opinions and wishes.

targets.label: A limited present subjunctive toolkit
targets.explanation: Essere gives sia, siamo, siate, siano; avere gives abbia, abbiamo, abbiate, abbiano in present subjunctive. Present subjunctive of -are uses -i (parli, ascolti); -ere/-ire uses -a (prenda, parta). Common irregulars include venga and possa.

repair.title: Try a limited present subjunctive toolkit again
repair.body: Essere gives sia, siamo, siate, siano; avere gives abbia, abbiamo, abbiate, abbiano in present subjunctive. Present subjunctive of -are uses -i (parli, ascolti); -ere/-ire uses -a (prenda, parta). Common irregulars include venga and possa.

examples.it: Penso che Sara sia pronta e che abbia tempo.
examples.en: I think Sara is ready and has time.

lessons.title: I think, I doubt
lessons.outcome: I can use the present subjunctive after uncertain opinions.

targets.label: I think, I doubt
targets.explanation: Penso che and credo che commonly introduce a present subjunctive when making a personal judgment. Dubito che and non sono sicuro che also invite the subjunctive.

repair.title: Try i think, i doubt again
repair.body: Penso che and credo che commonly introduce a present subjunctive when making a personal judgment. Dubito che and non sono sicuro che also invite the subjunctive.

examples.it: Penso che Maria sia a casa.
examples.en: I think Maria is at home.

lessons.title: Wishes and reactions
lessons.outcome: I can express what I want or feel about another person’s action.

targets.label: Wishes and reactions
targets.explanation: When I want someone else to act, volere che takes a subjunctive clause. Sono contento che and mi dispiace che express a reaction to another situation.

repair.title: Try wishes and reactions again
repair.body: When I want someone else to act, volere che takes a subjunctive clause. Sono contento che and mi dispiace che express a reaction to another situation.

examples.it: Voglio che tu venga con noi.
examples.en: I want you to come with us.

lessons.title: It is important that
lessons.outcome: I can make an impersonal evaluation with che and a subjunctive.

targets.label: It is important that
targets.explanation: È importante che, è necessario che and è possibile che introduce a subjunctive clause. È importante partire presto needs no che clause if no separate subject is named.

repair.title: Try it is important that again
repair.body: È importante che, è necessario che and è possibile che introduce a subjunctive clause. È importante partire presto needs no che clause if no separate subject is named.

examples.it: È importante che tutti capiscano.
examples.en: It is important that everyone understands.

units.title: Relay a message
units.description: Report statements, embed questions and preserve a speaker’s meaning.

lessons.title: Say what someone said
lessons.outcome: I can report a statement with dire che and a clear point of view.

targets.label: Say what someone said
targets.explanation: Dire che introduces the content of a statement. Adjust pronouns to the new speaker. When the reporting verb is present and the fact remains current, the subordinate often keeps its indicative tense.

repair.title: Try say what someone said again
repair.body: Dire che introduces the content of a statement. Adjust pronouns to the new speaker. When the reporting verb is present and the fact remains current, the subordinate often keeps its indicative tense.

examples.it: Marta dice: «Sono stanca». → Marta dice che è stanca.
examples.en: Marta says she is tired.

lessons.title: Ask what someone knows
lessons.outcome: I can embed a yes/no or wh-question after a reporting verb.

targets.label: Ask what someone knows
targets.explanation: A direct yes/no question becomes a clause with se after chiedere or sapere. Dove, quando and perché stay at the start of the embedded question; no question mark is needed in a statement.

repair.title: Try ask what someone knows again
repair.body: A direct yes/no question becomes a clause with se after chiedere or sapere. Dove, quando and perché stay at the start of the embedded question; no question mark is needed in a statement.

examples.it: Mi chiede: «Parti?» → Mi chiede se parto.
examples.en: She asks me whether I am leaving.

lessons.title: Relay a short message
lessons.outcome: I can pass on a short voicemail without changing the facts.

targets.label: Relay a short message
targets.explanation: Name who said the information. Forse remains uncertainty; a request to call back is still a request.

repair.title: Try relay a short message again
repair.body: Name who said the information. Forse remains uncertainty; a request to call back is still a request.

examples.it: Sara dice che arriverà alle sei.
examples.en: Sara says she will arrive at six.

steps.title: Relay a voicemail to a colleague

units.title: Read rules and write back
units.description: Understand general rules and simple passive service notices.

lessons.title: People in general
lessons.outcome: I can express a general habit or rule with impersonal si.

targets.label: People in general
targets.explanation: Si plus a third-person verb can mean people in general or one. Si è plus a plural adjective for a generic group: quando si è stanchi.

repair.title: Try people in general again
repair.body: Si plus a third-person verb can mean people in general or one. Si è plus a plural adjective for a generic group: quando si è stanchi.

examples.it: In Italia si cena spesso tardi.
examples.en: In Italy people often eat dinner late.

lessons.title: What receives the action
lessons.outcome: I can make a present or completed passive statement.

targets.label: What receives the action
targets.explanation: Passive essere plus past participle makes the object of an active verb the grammatical subject. The actor can follow da, and the participle agrees with the new subject.

repair.title: Try what receives the action again
repair.body: Passive essere plus past participle makes the object of an active verb the grammatical subject. The actor can follow da, and the participle agrees with the new subject.

examples.it: Il museo viene aperto alle nove.
examples.en: The museum is opened at nine.

lessons.title: Read and answer a rule
lessons.outcome: I can extract the action required by a short public notice and reply clearly.

targets.label: Read and answer a rule
targets.explanation: Non si entra means people may not enter. The passive can state what must happen to the document.

repair.title: Try read and answer a rule again
repair.body: Non si entra means people may not enter. The passive can state what must happen to the document.

examples.it: Qui non si entra dopo le otto.
examples.en: No one may enter here after eight.

units.title: Agree and connect
units.description: Agree the participle with a preceding object pronoun, refer to everyone and everything, and link reasons to their consequences.

lessons.title: Agree with lo, la, li and le
lessons.outcome: I can make the past participle agree with lo, la, li or le placed before avere, and leave it unchanged when the object follows the verb.

targets.label: Agree with lo, la, li and le
targets.explanation: When lo or la stands before ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete or hanno, it becomes l’ and the past participle takes the ending of that object: -o for lo, -a for la. Li gives -i and le gives -e. These plural pronouns keep their vowel: li ho, le ho. When the object follows the verb as a noun, nothing stands before ho and the participle keeps its basic -o form.

repair.title: Try agree with lo, la, li and le again
repair.body: When lo or la stands before ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete or hanno, it becomes l’ and the past participle takes the ending of that object: -o for lo, -a for la. Li gives -i and le gives -e. These plural pronouns keep their vowel: li ho, le ho. When the object follows the verb as a noun, nothing stands before ho and the participle keeps its basic -o form.

examples.it: Hai visto Marta? Sì, l’ho vista ieri.
examples.en: Did you see Marta? Yes, I saw her yesterday.

steps.title: Report what you have dealt with

lessons.title: Everyone, everything, everywhere
lessons.outcome: I can use ognuno, ciascuno, tutti, tutto, ovunque and dappertutto with the right verb agreement.

targets.label: Everyone, everything, everywhere
targets.explanation: Ognuno (ognuna for a group of women) and ciascuno mean each one taken singly, so the verb and any possessive are singular. Tutti (tutte for a group of women) means everyone or all of them and takes a plural verb; with essere, the participle agrees too. Tutto means everything and takes a singular verb; ovunque and dappertutto both mean everywhere and usually follow the verb.

repair.title: Try everyone, everything, everywhere again
repair.body: Ognuno (ognuna for a group of women) and ciascuno mean each one taken singly, so the verb and any possessive are singular. Tutti (tutte for a group of women) means everyone or all of them and takes a plural verb; with essere, the participle agrees too. Tutto means everything and takes a singular verb; ovunque and dappertutto both mean everywhere and usually follow the verb.

examples.it: Ognuno ha il suo posto. Ognuna di noi porta un dolce.
examples.en: Everyone has their own seat. Each of us brings a dessert.

lessons.title: Give the reason first
lessons.outcome: I can open a sentence with siccome, poiché or dato che, give a reason with perché after the main clause, and state a consequence with perciò or quindi.

targets.label: Give the reason first
targets.explanation: When the reason opens the sentence, use siccome, poiché or dato che, then give the result in the main clause. Perché does not open a statement this way. When the result comes first, the reason follows it with perché. State the fact as its own clause, then introduce what follows from it with perciò or quindi.

repair.title: Try give the reason first again
repair.body: When the reason opens the sentence, use siccome, poiché or dato che, then give the result in the main clause. Perché does not open a statement this way. When the result comes first, the reason follows it with perché. State the fact as its own clause, then introduce what follows from it with perciò or quindi.

examples.it: Siccome pioveva, sono rimasto a casa.
examples.en: Since it was raining, I stayed at home.

units.title: Everyday independence checkpoint
units.description: Apply connected narration, listening, problem solving and mediation in practical situations.

lessons.title: Explain a delayed arrival
lessons.outcome: I can give a coherent account of a delay, prior cause and outcome.

targets.label: Explain a delayed arrival
targets.explanation: The listener needs to know what was happening. Trapassato gives what had happened before; then say what you did.

repair.title: Try explain a delayed arrival again
repair.body: The listener needs to know what was happening. Trapassato gives what had happened before; then say what you did.

examples.it: Aspettavo il treno quando ho sentito l’annuncio.
examples.en: I was waiting for the train when I heard the announcement.

lessons.title: Hear and relay a changed arrangement
lessons.outcome: I can hear a practical change in a short message and pass on the exact detail.

targets.label: Hear and relay a changed arrangement
targets.explanation: The new arrangement usually follows non più or invece di. A useful relay says the new detail and, when needed, the condition.

repair.title: Try hear and relay a changed arrangement again
repair.body: The new arrangement usually follows non più or invece di. A useful relay says the new detail and, when needed, the condition.

examples.it: La visita non è più alle otto: comincia alle nove.
examples.en: The visit is no longer at eight: it begins at nine.

lessons.title: Resolve a service problem
lessons.outcome: I can state a problem, ask a specific question and propose a workable response.

targets.label: Resolve a service problem
targets.explanation: Give the staff member the key fact and the missing item. Use an embedded question and, if useful, an open condition.

repair.title: Try resolve a service problem again
repair.body: Give the staff member the key fact and the missing item. Use an embedded question and, if useful, an open condition.

examples.it: Ho una prenotazione, ma non trovo il modulo.
examples.en: I have a reservation, but I cannot find the form.

lessons.title: Pass on practical information
lessons.outcome: I can extract and summarize a substantial notice for someone who needs to act.

targets.label: Pass on practical information
targets.explanation: A notice may give both opening time and event time. Read which action each time belongs to. A condition can change one activity while another continues.

repair.title: Try pass on practical information again
repair.body: A notice may give both opening time and event time. Read which action each time belongs to. A condition can change one activity while another continues.

examples.it: La stazione apre alle sette; il treno parte alle otto.
examples.en: The station opens at seven; the train leaves at eight.

units.title: Fact and stance
units.description: Build productive present subjunctive patterns and distinguish known facts from viewpoints.

lessons.title: Build present subjunctive forms
lessons.outcome: I can make frequent regular present subjunctive forms across persons.

targets.label: Build present subjunctive forms
targets.explanation: Parlare gives parli for io/tu/lui/lei and parlino for loro; parliamo is noi. Prendere gives prenda/prendano; partire gives parta/partano.

repair.title: Try build present subjunctive forms again
repair.body: Parlare gives parli for io/tu/lui/lei and parlino for loro; parliamo is noi. Prendere gives prenda/prendano; partire gives parta/partano.

examples.it: Penso che Marta parli con Luca.
examples.en: I think Marta is talking to Luca.

lessons.title: Use frequent irregular subjunctives
lessons.outcome: I can select common irregular present subjunctive forms in a stated viewpoint.

targets.label: Use frequent irregular subjunctives
targets.explanation: Essere gives sia/siano; avere gives abbia/abbiano for singular/third plural. Andare gives vada/vadano; fare gives faccia/facciano.

repair.title: Try use frequent irregular subjunctives again
repair.body: Essere gives sia/siano; avere gives abbia/abbiano for singular/third plural. Andare gives vada/vadano; fare gives faccia/facciano.

examples.it: Credo che i ragazzi siano pronti e abbiano i biglietti.
examples.en: I think the boys are ready and have the tickets.

lessons.title: Separate fact from stance
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a stated fact from my evaluation of that fact.

targets.label: Separate fact from stance
targets.explanation: So che presents information the speaker takes as known. Temo che states concern, not evidence.

repair.title: Try separate fact from stance again
repair.body: So che presents information the speaker takes as known. Temo che states concern, not evidence.

examples.it: So che il museo è aperto oggi.
examples.en: I know the museum is open today.

units.title: Time inside a viewpoint
units.description: Relate an event to present or past attitudes by its actual temporal relation.

lessons.title: Earlier than a present judgment
lessons.outcome: I can use congiuntivo passato for an event completed before a current viewpoint.

targets.label: Earlier than a present judgment
targets.explanation: After penso che or temo che, use present subjunctive of the auxiliary plus participle for an earlier event. Movement and reflexive verbs use sia plus an agreeing participle.

repair.title: Try earlier than a present judgment again
repair.body: After penso che or temo che, use present subjunctive of the auxiliary plus participle for an earlier event. Movement and reflexive verbs use sia plus an agreeing participle.

examples.it: Penso che Anna abbia già finito.
examples.en: I think Anna has already finished.

lessons.title: Contemporary with a past viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can relate an ongoing event to a belief or feeling in the past.

targets.label: Contemporary with a past viewpoint
targets.explanation: Pensavo che or speravo che often takes imperfect subjunctive for a simultaneous or later event viewed from the past. The imperfect subjunctive keeps the event in the speaker’s viewpoint, without declaring it as a fact.

repair.title: Try contemporary with a past viewpoint again
repair.body: Pensavo che or speravo che often takes imperfect subjunctive for a simultaneous or later event viewed from the past. The imperfect subjunctive keeps the event in the speaker’s viewpoint, without declaring it as a fact.

examples.it: Pensavo che tu fossi a casa.
examples.en: I thought you were at home.

lessons.title: Earlier than a past viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can show an event was already over when someone formed a past belief.

targets.label: Earlier than a past viewpoint
targets.explanation: After a past opinion, use imperfect subjunctive auxiliary plus participle for an even earlier event. With essere, the participle agrees with the subordinate subject.

repair.title: Try earlier than a past viewpoint again
repair.body: After a past opinion, use imperfect subjunctive auxiliary plus participle for an even earlier event. With essere, the participle agrees with the subordinate subject.

examples.it: Pensavo che Anna fosse già partita.
examples.en: I thought Anna had already left.

lessons.title: Choose the time relationship
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish simultaneous, earlier and later events inside a past viewpoint.

targets.label: Choose the time relationship
targets.explanation: Pensavo che fosse in casa refers to then; pensavo che fosse uscito says he had left before then. The imperfect subjunctive can also express an event expected later from a past viewpoint, often with a future time marker.

repair.title: Try choose the time relationship again
repair.body: Pensavo che fosse in casa refers to then; pensavo che fosse uscito says he had left before then. The imperfect subjunctive can also express an event expected later from a past viewpoint, often with a future time marker.

examples.it: Credevo che Marco fosse in treno.
examples.en: I thought Marco was on the train.

units.title: Real and unreal alternatives
units.description: Imagine a different present, then express unreal past outcomes and present consequences.

lessons.title: If things were different now
lessons.outcome: I can imagine a different present situation and its possible result.

targets.label: If I had more time
targets.explanation: Use se plus imperfect subjunctive to present a contrary-to-fact or unlikely condition. The other clause takes present conditional. Do not put a conditional immediately after se in this standard pattern.

repair.title: Try if i had more time again
repair.body: Use se plus imperfect subjunctive to present a contrary-to-fact or unlikely condition. The other clause takes present conditional. Do not put a conditional immediately after se in this standard pattern.

examples.it: Se avessi più tempo, leggerei di più.
examples.en: If I had more time, I would read more.

lessons.title: Would have done
lessons.outcome: I can state an unreal past result or polite retrospective judgment.

targets.label: Would have done

lessons.title: Shorter clauses with an infinitive
lessons.outcome: I can use an infinitive when the subject relationship is clear.

lessons.title: While doing or by doing

targets.explanation: These constructions express that an action feels unavoidable, but differ from a bare physical inability.

repair.title: Revisit obligation and inevitability
repair.body: Non resta che introduces the remaining course of action.

examples.it: Non resta che aspettare.
examples.en: All that remains is to wait.

lessons.title: Proportional comparisons
lessons.outcome: I can link two changing quantities.

targets.label: Use più ... più ... to express parallel change
targets.explanation: Each più starts one comparative clause; the pattern relates their changes rather than comparing two static items.

repair.title: Revisit proportional comparisons
repair.body: The pattern can also pair less with more.

examples.it: Meno dormo, più sono stanco.
examples.en: The less I sleep, the more tired I am.

units.title: Hear stance and implication
units.description: Use a literary recording and an interview transcript to separate what is said from what is suggested.

lessons.title: Hear the narrator’s changing stance
lessons.outcome: I can follow an extended narrator’s correction of the listener’s first interpretation.

targets.label: Track a narrator’s stance across an excerpt
targets.explanation: In a narrative, a suggested explanation may later be qualified or withdrawn. Track whose inference it was and what later words do to it. In another account, a witness might say a closed door suggested a cancelled meeting, then learn that the meeting moved upstairs. Literary spellings such as neppur are for recognition in context.

repair.title: Check the source and the claim
repair.body: In a narrative, a suggested explanation may later be qualified or withdrawn. Track whose inference it was and what later words do to it. In another account, a witness might say a closed door suggested a cancelled meeting, then learn that the meeting moved upstairs. Literary spellings such as neppur are for recognition in context.

examples.it: La porta chiusa mi fece pensare che la riunione fosse annullata; poi seppi che si era spostata al piano superiore.
examples.en: The closed door made me think the meeting was cancelled; then I learned it had moved upstairs.

lessons.title: Read what an interviewee leaves implied
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish an interviewee’s answer from the interviewer’s suggested conclusion.

targets.label: Interpret an interview exchange without overclaiming
targets.explanation: An interviewer may put a conclusion into a question. The interviewee can narrow, qualify or reject that premise. Report the answer that was given, not the assumption carried by the question.

repair.title: Check the source and the claim
repair.body: An interviewer may put a conclusion into a question. The interviewee can narrow, qualify or reject that premise. Report the answer that was given, not the assumption carried by the question.

examples.it: «Quindi il progetto è fallito?» «Direi piuttosto che la prima fase è durata più del previsto.»
examples.en: “So the project failed?” “I would rather say that the first phase took longer than expected.”

units.title: Manage discussion
units.description: Put the disputed point in focus and restate an objection faithfully.

lessons.title: Cleft focus and contrast
lessons.outcome: I can highlight the one person or thing that matters.

targets.label: Use è ... che to focus a constituent and express contrast
targets.explanation: A cleft presents one element as the new, contrastive focus.

repair.title: Revisit cleft focus and contrast
repair.body: The highlighted item may be an object too.

examples.it: È questo libro che cerco.
examples.en: It is this book that I am looking for.

lessons.title: Correction without contradiction
lessons.outcome: I can replace an imprecise claim with a better one.

targets.label: Use non tanto ... quanto ... to shift emphasis from one description to another
targets.explanation: The pattern does not always fully deny the first element; it foregrounds the second as more accurate.

repair.title: Revisit correction without contradiction
repair.body: Keep the two compared phrases grammatically parallel.

examples.it: Non tanto per il costo quanto per il tempo.
examples.en: Not so much because of the cost as because of the time.

units.title: Write for an institution
units.description: Choose formal distance without obscuring who requests or decides.

lessons.title: Conditional requests and reported claims
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a polite request from an unverified report.

targets.label: Read the conditional from its communicative setting
targets.explanation: Vorrei softens a request; a journalistic conditional can distance the writer from an unverified claim.

repair.title: Revisit conditional requests and reported claims
repair.body: The conditional can signal that a claim is reported rather than verified.

examples.it: Il ministro sarebbe arrivato ieri.
examples.en: The minister reportedly arrived yesterday.

lessons.title: Impersonal and passive si
lessons.outcome: I can avoid an unnecessary agent in formal information.

targets.label: Use impersonal si for general activity and passive si with plural agreement when a plural object becomes subject
targets.explanation: Si lavora is impersonal; si cercano volontari is a passive construction whose verb agrees with volontari.

repair.title: Revisit impersonal and passive si
repair.body: With passive si, a plural patient controls plural agreement.

examples.it: Si cercano volontari.
examples.en: Volunteers are being sought.

units.title: Synthesize sources
units.description: Keep references and connections clear when two accounts only partly agree.

lessons.title: Clear anaphoric reference
lessons.outcome: I can refer back to the intended item in a two-item sequence.

targets.label: Choose il primo or il secondo when pronouns would be ambiguous
targets.explanation: This lesson uses explicit ordinal reference so the antecedent is recoverable without guesswork.

repair.title: Revisit clear anaphoric reference
repair.body: Repeat or label an antecedent when it matters.

examples.it: Marta ha parlato con Anna. Anna era preoccupata.
examples.en: Marta spoke to Anna. Anna was worried.

lessons.title: Contrast and consequence
lessons.outcome: I can choose a connector that preserves the argument.

targets.label: Distinguish tuttavia from pertanto in linked claims
targets.explanation: Tuttavia introduces a contrast; pertanto introduces a consequence.

repair.title: Revisit contrast and consequence
repair.body: Pertanto draws an outcome from what came before.

examples.it: Il treno è fermo; pertanto, arriveremo tardi.
examples.en: The train has stopped; therefore, we will arrive late.

targets.label: Distinguish two spoken accounts of the delay
targets.explanation: Two accounts of the same event can describe different observations. Keep each speaker’s direct knowledge apart from an inferred cause. For example, one witness may know when a bell rang, while another has the maintenance log; neither alone proves why the alarm sounded.

repair.title: Listen for the attributed detail
repair.body: Two accounts of the same event can describe different observations. Keep each speaker’s direct knowledge apart from an inferred cause. For example, one witness may know when a bell rang, while another has the maintenance log; neither alone proves why the alarm sounded.

examples.it: Ho sentito la campana alle otto, ma non so perché sia suonata.
examples.en: I heard the bell at eight, but I do not know why it rang.

steps.title: Brief a passenger from three accounts

units.title: Put C1 together
units.description: Turn a complex report into concise, appropriately qualified prose.

lessons.title: Actions as nouns
lessons.outcome: I can turn a full action clause into a concise noun phrase.

targets.label: Use a clear event noun and preserve its participants
targets.explanation: Nominalization can foreground an event, but the agent or object should remain recoverable.

repair.title: Revisit actions as nouns
repair.body: A noun phrase can retain who acted with da parte di.

examples.it: L’approvazione del piano da parte del consiglio è attesa.
examples.en: Approval of the plan by the council is expected.

lessons.title: Compact formal clauses
lessons.outcome: I can shorten a time or condition clause without losing the logical link.

targets.label: Use a precise preposition and noun phrase for a compact formal relation
targets.explanation: A compact formal phrase must preserve whether it means after, before or on condition.

repair.title: Revisit compact formal clauses
repair.body: In caso di + noun marks a condition, not a cause.

examples.it: In caso di ritardo, avvisateci.
examples.en: In case of delay, let us know.

targets.label: Reconcile volunteer and treasurer accounts
targets.explanation: A registration count, an activity count and a financial estimate answer different questions. Listen for which speaker can substantiate each number, and keep a proposal for next year separate from a measured outcome. In a different project, forty tickets sold would not establish forty people attended.

repair.title: Listen for the attributed detail
repair.body: A registration count, an activity count and a financial estimate answer different questions. Listen for which speaker can substantiate each number, and keep a proposal for next year separate from a measured outcome. In a different project, forty tickets sold would not establish forty people attended.

examples.it: Sono stati venduti quaranta biglietti; le presenze effettive non sono ancora state contate.
examples.en: Forty tickets were sold; actual attendance has not yet been counted.

units.title: Nuanced grammatical choices
units.description: Judge how mood and aspect change the speaker’s commitment.

lessons.title: Evidence and speaker stance
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish an asserted fact from a speaker’s inference.

targets.label: Use an indicative assertion or a subjunctive evaluation according to the matrix clause
targets.explanation: C2 control includes choosing a mood for stance, not applying one mechanical rule to every che-clause.

repair.title: Revisit evidence and speaker stance
repair.body: È possibile che places the event in the realm of possibility.

examples.it: È possibile che il treno sia partito.
examples.en: It is possible that the train has left.

lessons.title: Event boundary and viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can choose a past form to foreground an event or its background.

targets.label: Use passato prossimo for a bounded event and imperfetto for the ongoing background in this context
targets.explanation: The same real-world episode can be packaged differently according to the narrative viewpoint.

repair.title: Revisit event boundary and viewpoint
repair.body: Passato prossimo presents a completed occurrence.

examples.it: Ha piovuto tutta la notte.
examples.en: It rained all night.

units.title: Advanced hypotheticals
units.description: Track mixed time and implied conditions without turning possibility into fact.

lessons.title: Unreal past conditions
lessons.outcome: I can state an unreal past condition and its unreal result.

targets.label: Use se + trapassato congiuntivo with a past conditional result
targets.explanation: The result is counterfactual because the stated past condition did not happen.

repair.title: Revisit unreal past conditions
repair.body: The apodosis takes a past conditional for the unreal outcome.

examples.it: Se fossimo partiti prima, avremmo preso il treno.
examples.en: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.

lessons.title: Past cause, present result
lessons.outcome: I can connect an unreal past condition to a present state.

targets.label: Use a past subjunctive condition with a present conditional result when the result is now
targets.explanation: A mixed conditional locates the unreal cause in the past and its consequence in the present.

repair.title: Revisit past cause, present result
repair.body: The result is a present state, so use the present conditional.

examples.it: Se avessimo studiato, oggi sapremmo rispondere.
examples.en: If we had studied, we would know how to answer today.

targets.label: Separate lost and live options in two speakers
targets.explanation: A missed past opportunity and a live present option can be discussed in the same conversation. Classify each conditional by its timeline, and do not turn a counterfactual possibility into a guaranteed result. For example, a cancelled visit last year does not decide whether a new visit can be arranged now.

repair.title: Listen for the attributed detail
repair.body: A missed past opportunity and a live present option can be discussed in the same conversation. Classify each conditional by its timeline, and do not turn a counterfactual possibility into a guaranteed result. For example, a cancelled visit last year does not decide whether a new visit can be arranged now.

examples.it: Se fossimo partiti ieri, avremmo visto la mostra; oggi possiamo ancora prenotare un’altra visita.
examples.en: If we had left yesterday, we would have seen the exhibition; today we can still book another visit.

steps.title: Explain the two timelines to the board

units.title: Precision and ambiguity
units.description: Repair reference and scope where a plausible reading changes the claim.

lessons.title: Resolve competing antecedents
lessons.outcome: I can remove a pronoun ambiguity in a short text.

targets.label: Repeat a name or role when two referents could fit a pronoun
targets.explanation: In precise prose, explicit reference often serves better than a formally grammatical but unclear pronoun.

repair.title: Revisit resolve competing antecedents
repair.body: Name the intended person in the second clause.

examples.it: Paolo ha scritto a Marco. Marco era preoccupato.
examples.en: Paolo wrote to Marco. Marco was worried.

lessons.title: Quantifier scope under negation
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish “not all” from “none.”

targets.label: Use non tutti for a partial negative and nessuno for a total negative
targets.explanation: The placement of negation changes the logical claim; non tutti leaves open that some did.

repair.title: Revisit quantifier scope under negation
repair.body: Nessuno means zero members.

examples.it: Nessun ospite è arrivato.
examples.en: No guest arrived.

units.title: Ellipsis and implication
units.description: Recover omitted material and notice assumptions embedded in a question.

lessons.title: Parallel ellipsis
lessons.outcome: I can omit a repeated verb without hiding the relationship.

targets.label: In balanced clauses, omit a recoverable repeated verb and keep the two parts parallel
targets.explanation: A comma may mark the place of an omitted verb in compact edited prose.

repair.title: Revisit parallel ellipsis
repair.body: The omitted verb must fit the second clause too.

examples.it: Io porto il pane; tu, l’acqua.
examples.en: I will bring the bread; you, the water.

lessons.title: Implications of aspect verbs
lessons.outcome: I can infer what smettere and riprendere imply.

targets.label: Recognize the earlier activity implied by smettere and riprendere
targets.explanation: Smettere di X implies X occurred before; riprendere a X implies X occurred earlier and was interrupted.

repair.title: Revisit implications of aspect verbs
repair.body: Riprendere a presupposes an earlier phase and interruption.

examples.it: Marta ha ripreso a correre.
examples.en: Marta has started running again.

units.title: Literary and historical language
units.description: Hear a narrator address readers and recognize older forms in their own context.

lessons.title: Hear a narrator unsettle the reader
lessons.outcome: I can track how a literary narrator uses reader address, interruption and expectation.

targets.label: Interpret a narrator’s intervention
targets.explanation: A storyteller can address readers, supply an expected response and then disturb that expectation. Notice who offers each answer and how the narrator changes the reader’s position. For example, “Vi aspettavate il tesoro? La scatola era vuota” reverses an expectation without explaining the whole mystery. Older forms belong to their literary setting; recognition does not require using them in an everyday message.

repair.title: Check the source and the claim
repair.body: A storyteller can address readers, supply an expected response and then disturb that expectation. Notice who offers each answer and how the narrator changes the reader’s position. For example, “Vi aspettavate il tesoro? La scatola era vuota” reverses an expectation without explaining the whole mystery. Older forms belong to their literary setting; recognition does not require using them in an everyday message.

examples.it: Vi aspettavate il tesoro? La scatola era vuota.
examples.en: Were you expecting the treasure? The box was empty.

lessons.title: Narrative past and present relevance
lessons.outcome: I can recognize the narrative function of passato remoto.

targets.label: Use passato remoto for a closed historical narrative when the task asks for that style
targets.explanation: Passato prossimo also occurs in Italian narratives; this lesson fixes the intended written register explicitly.

repair.title: Revisit narrative past and present relevance
repair.body: Passato prossimo often suits a current report about a recent event.

examples.it: Oggi il Parlamento ha approvato la legge.
examples.en: Today Parliament approved the law.

units.title: Contemporary variation and register
units.description: Recognize spoken variation and choose a register for an audience.

lessons.title: Spoken dislocation in context
lessons.outcome: I can identify a spoken topic structure and recast it for a formal text.

targets.label: Recognize clitic resumption as common in conversation; choose a neutral order for formal editing when needed
targets.explanation: Spoken “a me mi” is a marked topicalization; formal prose can say “a me piace” or use a neutral clause.

repair.title: Revisit spoken dislocation in context
repair.body: A more neutral written form can omit the repeated clitic.

examples.it: A me piace questa idea.
examples.en: I like this idea.

lessons.title: Match request to audience
lessons.outcome: I can rewrite a direct request for a formal recipient while preserving the request.

targets.label: Use a courteous conditional and a clear request complement in formal correspondence
targets.explanation: Formal tone comes from grammar and framing as well as word choice.

repair.title: Revisit match request to audience
repair.body: Potrebbe + infinitive makes the same request more courteous.

examples.it: Potrebbe inviarmi il documento?
examples.en: Could you send me the document?

units.title: Edit a complex text
units.description: Restore cohesion, parallel structure and evidence in a dense draft.

lessons.title: Repair a false logical link
lessons.outcome: I can replace a connector that misstates the relation between claims.

targets.label: Choose a connector from the actual logic, not from surface punctuation
targets.explanation: A misleading connective can make a grammatical text incoherent.

repair.title: Revisit repair a false logical link
repair.body: Eppure signals an outcome contrary to expectation.

examples.it: La strada è lunga; eppure arriviamo presto.
examples.en: The road is long; yet we arrive early.

lessons.title: Parallel clauses in edited prose
lessons.outcome: I can repair an uneven pair of coordinated complements.

targets.label: Give coordinated items the same grammatical form when they play the same role
targets.explanation: Parallelism makes a comparison or list easier to parse without changing its meaning.

repair.title: Revisit parallel clauses in edited prose
repair.body: Repeat a governing preposition when it helps symmetry and clarity.

examples.it: Puntiamo a capire il problema e a risolverlo.
examples.en: We aim to understand the problem and solve it.

units.title: Interpret competing readings
units.description: Follow irony and older constructions without importing an invented motive.

lessons.title: Read stance across two sentences
lessons.outcome: I can identify what is asserted and what remains a possibility.

targets.label: Track both source marking and grammatical mood across a short report
targets.explanation: A conditional attributed to a source reports a claim; an indicative confirmation asserts verified information.

repair.title: Revisit read stance across two sentences
repair.body: A later confirmation can switch to indicative.

examples.it: L’ufficio ha confermato che si è dimesso.
examples.en: The office confirmed that he resigned.

lessons.title: Marked order in literary narration
lessons.outcome: I can interpret a literary subject placed after the verb.

targets.label: Recognize verb–subject order as a way of introducing a new actor in a narrative scene
targets.explanation: In this context, the postverbal noun remains the subject, not the object.

repair.title: Revisit marked order in literary narration
repair.body: A neutral paraphrase can put the subject first.

examples.it: Il messaggero entrò.
examples.en: The messenger entered.

units.title: Evaluate sources and inference
units.description: Decide which wording remains justified when reports disagree.

lessons.title: Degrees of inference
lessons.outcome: I can express strong or tentative inference about an earlier action.

targets.label: Distinguish deve aver + participle from potrebbe aver + participle
targets.explanation: Deve aver marks a strong inference in context; potrebbe aver leaves more room for alternatives.

repair.title: Revisit degrees of inference
repair.body: Potrebbe aver presents a possible explanation.

examples.it: Potrebbe aver perso le chiavi.
examples.en: He may have lost the keys.

lessons.title: Possession in relative clauses
lessons.outcome: I can express whose item is involved without a vague pronoun.

targets.label: Use il cui / la cui + possessed noun with agreement to the possessed noun
targets.explanation: Cui itself is invariable; the article agrees with the noun that follows, not with the antecedent.

repair.title: Revisit possession in relative clauses
repair.body: La cui firma agrees with firma.

examples.it: La donna la cui firma manca è assente.
examples.en: The woman whose signature is missing is absent.

units.title: Mediate conflicting sources
units.description: Preserve caveats and adapt a synthesis to an audience’s actual decision.

lessons.title: Reconcile three partial accounts
lessons.outcome: I can identify what three sources do and do not establish about one policy choice.

targets.label: Synthesize without flattening disagreement
targets.explanation: Different sources can measure journeys, report a need or describe an objection without answering the same question. Attribute each claim and ask what joint decision remains unsupported. For example, a count of museum entries does not reveal why visitors came or whether a new entrance is needed.

repair.title: Check the source and the claim
repair.body: Different sources can measure journeys, report a need or describe an objection without answering the same question. Attribute each claim and ask what joint decision remains unsupported. For example, a count of museum entries does not reveal why visitors came or whether a new entrance is needed.

examples.it: Le entrate misurano gli accessi al museo, non il motivo della visita.
examples.en: Entry counts measure visits to the museum, not the reason for each visit.

lessons.title: Adapt the same evidence to two audiences
lessons.outcome: I can brief riders and decision-makers without changing the facts or their certainty.

targets.label: Preserve evidence across audiences
targets.explanation: A rider needs to know what might change and when; a council needs the evidence limits and trial design. Both versions must preserve the uncertainty about effects on the hospital and the neighbourhood.

repair.title: Check the source and the claim
repair.body: A rider needs to know what might change and when; a council needs the evidence limits and trial design. Both versions must preserve the uncertainty about effects on the hospital and the neighbourhood.

examples.it: La deviazione è una proposta; prima di una decisione definitiva verrà valutata con una prova.
examples.en: The diversion is a proposal; it will be evaluated in a trial before a final decision.

units.title: Implicit conditions and compression
units.description: Interpret unstated conditions and condense dense prose without losing logical links.

lessons.title: Conditions without se
lessons.outcome: I can recognize an implied condition in a compact phrase.

targets.label: Read senza + noun or con + noun as an implicit hypothetical when paired with a conditional
targets.explanation: An implicit phrase can stand for a fuller if-clause; the conditional shows its hypothetical status.

repair.title: Revisit conditions without se
repair.body: Senza il tuo aiuto can mean if I did not have your help.

examples.it: Senza il tuo aiuto, non riuscirei.
examples.en: Without your help, I would not manage.

lessons.title: Compress without hiding an agent
lessons.outcome: I can condense a clause while keeping who did what clear.

targets.label: Use nominalization with a named agent when it is needed for meaning
targets.explanation: A shorter noun phrase is useful only if the performer and affected item stay recoverable.

repair.title: Revisit compress without hiding an agent
repair.body: A finite clause can restore the agent if a nominal phrase becomes opaque.

examples.it: Il consiglio ha approvato il piano.
examples.en: The council approved the plan.

units.title: Put C2 together
units.description: Interpret several sources and produce precise responses for different audiences.

lessons.title: Choose a precise final wording
lessons.outcome: I can produce a concise, logically precise sentence for a specified audience.

targets.label: Combine condition, consequence and register in a single short rewrite
targets.explanation: Check the intended relation and recipient before choosing the grammatical form.

repair.title: Revisit choose a precise final wording
repair.body: A formal request can use a conditional question.

examples.it: Potrebbe confermarmi il nuovo orario?
examples.en: Could you confirm the new time for me?

lessons.title: Synthesize a contested dossier
lessons.outcome: I can compare three partial sources and recommend a decision process without erasing limits.

targets.label: Interpret and mediate a complex dossier
targets.explanation: When several documents describe one choice, each estimate has a source and conditions. Identify what each source actually establishes, then recommend a measurement that resolves a decision-relevant gap. For example, a quiet road observed at noon need not be quiet at school opening time.

repair.title: Check the source and the claim
repair.body: When several documents describe one choice, each estimate has a source and conditions. Identify what each source actually establishes, then recommend a measurement that resolves a decision-relevant gap. For example, a quiet road observed at noon need not be quiet at school opening time.

examples.it: La strada era poco trafficata a mezzogiorno; per decidere sull’ingresso scolastico servono dati nell’orario pertinente.
examples.en: The road had little traffic at noon; deciding on the school entrance needs data from the relevant time.

targets.label: Compare an accessibility account with a service proposal
targets.explanation: Travel-time figures can measure only part of a journey. Check the route, user, waiting time and conditions behind each estimate before comparing alternatives. A three-minute lift ride, for example, says little about access if the lift does not reach the entrance.

repair.title: Listen for the attributed detail
repair.body: Travel-time figures can measure only part of a journey. Check the route, user, waiting time and conditions behind each estimate before comparing alternatives. A three-minute lift ride, for example, says little about access if the lift does not reach the entrance.

examples.it: La corsa in ascensore dura tre minuti, ma il tempo di accesso all’ingresso resta da misurare.
examples.en: The lift ride takes three minutes, but access time to the entrance still needs measuring.

lessons.title: Say what you have

lessons.title: Recognize noun gender

lessons.outcome: I can choose un, uno, una, or un’ in a new-item phrase.

lessons.title: Name known things
lessons.outcome: I can choose singular and plural definite articles, including lo and gli.

lessons.outcome: I can form regular noun plurals and keep the article in agreement.

lessons.title: Describe a noun
lessons.outcome: I can make a common adjective agree in gender and number.

lessons.title: Use -ere verbs now

lessons.title: Point to this or that
lessons.outcome: I can use common questo and quello forms with a nearby or distant noun.

lessons.title: Choose a basic preposition

lessons.title: Combine a preposition and article

lessons.title: Say what you like
