units.title: Completed past
units.description: Tell a short account of completed actions with the right auxiliary and participle.

lessons.title: Build regular completed past
lessons.outcome: I can form passato prossimo with avere and regular participles across three verb families.

lessons.title: Use essere in the past
lessons.outcome: I can form passato prossimo with essere and make its participle agree with the subject.

lessons.title: Recall common participles
lessons.outcome: I can use frequent irregular participles for completed events.

lessons.title: Choose the past auxiliary
lessons.outcome: I can choose the auxiliary from a verb’s pattern, including common movement exceptions.

units.title: Past background and action in progress
units.description: Show what used to happen, what happened once, and what was in progress.

lessons.title: Describe past habits and states
lessons.outcome: I can form common imperfect forms for repeated actions and background states.

lessons.title: Contrast background and event
lessons.outcome: I can choose imperfect for an ongoing background and passato prossimo for a completed event.

lessons.title: Focus on an action now
lessons.outcome: I can use stare + gerund for an action in progress now and avoid it for ordinary habits.

lessons.title: Focus on an action underway then
lessons.outcome: I can use stavo/stava/stavamo + gerund for an action underway at a past moment.

objectives.label: Focus on an action underway then

units.title: Reflexives and small pronouns
units.description: Keep the right person or thing in view without repeating each noun.

lessons.title: Describe your own routine
lessons.outcome: I can use a reflexive pronoun with a present-tense daily-routine verb.

lessons.title: Tell a reflexive past event
lessons.outcome: I can use essere with a past reflexive verb and agree the participle.

lessons.title: Replace the thing seen
lessons.outcome: I can use lo, la, li, and le before a finite verb to avoid repeating a direct object.

lessons.title: Say to whom
lessons.outcome: I can use mi, ti, gli, and le for a receiver or addressee.

lessons.title: Place a pronoun with an infinitive
lessons.outcome: I can place a direct-object pronoun before a modal or attach it to the infinitive.

objectives.label: Place a pronoun with an infinitive

units.title: Future and polite possibilities
units.description: Make a future plan and soften a request with a conditional form.

lessons.title: Make a future plan
lessons.outcome: I can form the regular future of common -are, -ere, and -ire verbs.

lessons.title: Use common irregular futures
lessons.outcome: I can use future stems of essere, avere, andare, fare, and venire.

lessons.title: Ask more politely
lessons.outcome: I can use vorrei, potrei, and potrebbe in courteous requests and simple possibilities.

units.title: Compare and measure
units.description: Compare people and things, then describe a useful amount.

lessons.title: Compare two things
lessons.outcome: I can use più/meno ... di for two people or things and ... che for two qualities or actions.

lessons.title: Pick the highest degree
lessons.outcome: I can say “the most” in a group and intensify an adjective with -issimo.

lessons.title: Use approximate amounts
lessons.outcome: I can choose qualche, alcuni/alcune, troppo, and un po’ di with suitable nouns.

units.title: Commands, prepositions, and links
units.description: Give clear directions and connect two small ideas in a useful sentence.

lessons.title: Address one person politely
lessons.outcome: I can give a courteous Lei instruction with a common command form.

lessons.title: Tell someone not to do it
lessons.outcome: I can form a negative tu command and place an object pronoun naturally.

objectives.label: Tell someone not to do it

lessons.title: Use da for source, person, and duration
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish da for origin, visiting a person, and a duration continuing now.

objectives.label: Use da for source, person, and duration

lessons.title: Connect cause and sequence
lessons.outcome: I can link short ideas with perché, quindi, poi, and mentre.

lessons.title: Add one detail with che
lessons.outcome: I can join a noun to a simple describing clause with che.

units.title: Tell a connected story
units.description: Place background, completed events and earlier actions on one timeline.

lessons.title: Background meets event
lessons.outcome: I can set a scene and name the event that interrupted it.

lessons.title: Before another past event
lessons.outcome: I can show that one past action happened before another.

lessons.title: Repeated life in the past
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish an old routine from a single completed occasion.

units.title: Refer back without repeating
units.description: Combine small pronouns and replace places or quantities clearly.

lessons.title: Give it to someone
lessons.outcome: I can combine an indirect object pronoun with a direct one.

lessons.title: Ci for a place
lessons.outcome: I can refer back to a known place with ci.

lessons.title: Ne for some or of it
lessons.outcome: I can replace a previously named quantity or di phrase with ne.

objectives.label: Ne for some or of it

units.title: Join descriptions
units.description: Make smooth relative clauses with subject, object and prepositional links.

lessons.title: Che and cui
lessons.outcome: I can link a noun to a clause using che or cui.

lessons.title: The right preposition before cui
lessons.outcome: I can carry a verb’s required preposition into a relative clause.

units.title: Express a viewpoint
units.description: Use the present subjunctive after opinion, wishes and impersonal evaluation.

lessons.title: I think, I doubt
lessons.outcome: I can use the present subjunctive after uncertain opinions.

lessons.title: Wishes and reactions
lessons.outcome: I can express what I want or feel about another person’s action.

lessons.title: It is important that
lessons.outcome: I can make an impersonal evaluation with che and a subjunctive.

units.title: Say what depends on what
units.description: Distinguish likely conditions from imagined present situations.

lessons.title: If it happens
lessons.outcome: I can use se with an open, realistic condition.

lessons.title: If I had more time
lessons.outcome: I can imagine an unreal or unlikely present situation.

units.title: Pass information on
units.description: Report statements and embedded questions without changing their meaning.

lessons.title: Say what someone said
lessons.outcome: I can report a statement with dire che and a clear point of view.

lessons.title: Ask what someone knows
lessons.outcome: I can embed a yes/no or wh-question after a reporting verb.

units.title: Keep the focus on the action
units.description: Use impersonal and passive forms when the actor is general or secondary.

lessons.title: People in general
lessons.outcome: I can express a general habit or rule with impersonal si.

lessons.title: What receives the action
lessons.outcome: I can make a present or completed passive statement.

units.title: Link reasons and outcomes
units.description: Use clause links to explain purpose, results, contrast and event order.

lessons.title: Because or in order to
lessons.outcome: I can choose a reason or purpose clause according to meaning.

lessons.title: Result and surprise
lessons.outcome: I can link a result or a fact that contrasts with expectation.

lessons.title: Before and after
lessons.outcome: I can sequence actions and choose infinitive or finite clauses.

legacyLevels.title: B2 · Shape complex accounts and arguments

units.title: Manage viewpoint and time
units.description: Relate a subordinate event to the time of a belief, fear or judgment.

lessons.title: Earlier than a present judgment
lessons.outcome: I can use congiuntivo passato for an event completed before a current viewpoint.

lessons.title: Contemporary with a past viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can relate an ongoing event to a belief or feeling in the past.

lessons.title: Earlier than a past viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can show an event was already over when someone formed a past belief.

lessons.title: Choose the time relationship
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish simultaneous, earlier and later events inside a past viewpoint.

units.title: Reflect on unreal outcomes
units.description: Express unreal past situations, regrets and consequences still felt now.

lessons.title: Would have done
lessons.outcome: I can state an unreal past result or polite retrospective judgment.

lessons.title: If it had happened
lessons.outcome: I can link an unreal past condition to its unreal past result.

lessons.title: Past cause, present effect
lessons.outcome: I can connect an unreal past event to its consequence now.

units.title: Retell from a later viewpoint
units.description: Shift tense, time and person when reporting past speech or requests.

lessons.title: He said he was leaving
lessons.outcome: I can report a past statement with a past reporting verb.

lessons.title: Retell a question
lessons.outcome: I can report past questions and adjust their reference words.

lessons.title: Pass on an instruction
lessons.outcome: I can report an instruction with di plus infinitive.

units.title: Control agency
units.description: Choose passive form and agreement for what the sentence puts in focus.

lessons.title: Passive across time
lessons.outcome: I can keep passive voice while moving an event across tenses.

lessons.title: Things are sold here
lessons.outcome: I can use si passivante with a singular or plural thing being acted upon.

units.title: Compress and refine clauses
units.description: Use precise relatives and shorter infinitive or gerund clauses.

lessons.title: Clarify which noun you mean
lessons.outcome: I can choose il quale or ciò che when a simple che is unclear or has no noun to refer to.

lessons.title: Shorter clauses with an infinitive
lessons.outcome: I can use an infinitive when the subject relationship is clear.

lessons.title: While doing or by doing
lessons.outcome: I can use a gerund when the understood actor is the same.

units.title: Build an argument
units.description: Mark contrast, concession and logical progression in connected prose.

lessons.title: Despite the obstacle
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a factual contrast from a conceded possibility.

lessons.title: Guide a reader through a claim
lessons.outcome: I can mark an addition, consequence and counterpoint in an argument.

objectives.label: Guide a reader through a claim

units.title: Put information in focus
units.description: Change sentence structure to highlight or recover a known topic.

lessons.title: It was Marta who called
lessons.outcome: I can use è...che to focus the person, time or place that matters.

lessons.title: Return to a known topic
lessons.outcome: I can put a known object first and resume it with a pronoun.

units.title: Read and tell distant events
units.description: Recognize literary historical narration and the sequence before it.

lessons.title: A completed story event
lessons.outcome: I can recognize and use common passato remoto forms in a written story.

lessons.title: Before a remote past event
lessons.outcome: I can recognize trapassato remoto in a written historical sequence.

units.title: Mood and aspect in perspective
units.description: Choose forms that show stance, sequence and conjecture.

lessons.title: Facts, opinion and the subjunctive
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a reported fact from a speaker’s evaluation.

objectives.label: Switch mood when a clause is evaluated rather than asserted.

lessons.title: Time within past evaluations
lessons.outcome: I can place a subordinate event before or alongside a past viewpoint.

objectives.label: Choose imperfetto or trapassato congiuntivo from relative time.

lessons.title: Future forms as conjecture
lessons.outcome: I can use future forms to express a present or past guess.

objectives.label: Distinguish chronological future from epistemic future.

units.title: Relations between clauses
units.description: Mark concession, purpose and precise reference.

lessons.title: Concession with sebbene and pur
lessons.outcome: I can concede a fact without losing the main claim.

objectives.label: Use an explicit or implicit concessive form with the right subject.

lessons.title: Cause and purpose
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a reason from an intended result.

objectives.label: Choose perché, poiché or affinché with the intended relationship.

lessons.title: Precise relative links
lessons.outcome: I can link a relative clause to the intended noun.

objectives.label: Use preposition + cui or il quale to make the relationship explicit.

units.title: Infinitive, participle and gerund
units.description: Compress clauses while preserving time and subject.

lessons.title: Infinitive subjects and sequence
lessons.outcome: I can reduce a clause when its subject is understood.

objectives.label: Use di + infinitive after a same-subject verb; use a full che-clause when subjects differ.

lessons.title: Earlier action in reduced clauses
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish simultaneous from prior action in a reduced clause.

objectives.label: Use simple gerund for overlap, compound gerund or past participle for prior completion.

units.title: Topic and focus
units.description: Direct the reader’s attention without changing the facts.

lessons.title: Known topic and pronoun resumption
lessons.outcome: I can put a known object first and resume it clearly.

objectives.label: Recognize and form left dislocation with a matching clitic.

lessons.title: Cleft focus and contrast
lessons.outcome: I can highlight the one person or thing that matters.

objectives.label: Use è ... che to focus a constituent and express contrast.

units.title: Register and politeness
units.description: Make requests and reports fit their audience.

lessons.title: Conditional requests and reported claims
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a polite request from an unverified report.

objectives.label: Read the conditional from its communicative setting.

lessons.title: Impersonal and passive si
lessons.outcome: I can avoid an unnecessary agent in formal information.

objectives.label: Use impersonal si for general activity and passive si with plural agreement when a plural object becomes subject.

units.title: Cohesion and reference
units.description: Keep readers oriented across connected sentences.

lessons.title: Clear anaphoric reference
lessons.outcome: I can refer back to the intended item in a two-item sequence.

objectives.label: Choose il primo or il secondo when pronouns would be ambiguous.

lessons.title: Contrast and consequence
lessons.outcome: I can choose a connector that preserves the argument.

objectives.label: Distinguish tuttavia from pertanto in linked claims.

lessons.title: Time in reported speech
lessons.outcome: I can locate a future or earlier event from a past report.

objectives.label: Use past conditional for later-than-past and pluperfect for earlier-than-past.

units.title: Concise formal style
units.description: Turn actions into concise, readable formal statements.

lessons.title: Actions as nouns
lessons.outcome: I can turn a full action clause into a concise noun phrase.

objectives.label: Use a clear event noun and preserve its participants.

lessons.title: Compact formal clauses
lessons.outcome: I can shorten a time or condition clause without losing the logical link.

objectives.label: Use a precise preposition and noun phrase for a compact formal relation.

units.title: Idiomatic reformulation
units.description: Restate a point accurately with compact idiomatic patterns.

lessons.title: Obligation and inevitability
lessons.outcome: I can reformulate inevitability without changing its force.

objectives.label: Use non poter fare a meno di + infinitive or non restare che + infinitive appropriately.

lessons.title: Proportional comparisons
lessons.outcome: I can link two changing quantities.

objectives.label: Use più ... più ... to express parallel change.

lessons.title: Correction without contradiction
lessons.outcome: I can replace an imprecise claim with a better one.

objectives.label: Use non tanto ... quanto ... to shift emphasis from one description to another.

units.title: Nuanced grammatical choices
units.description: Choose forms by evidence, viewpoint and degree of certainty.

lessons.title: Evidence and speaker stance
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish an asserted fact from a speaker’s inference.

objectives.label: Use an indicative assertion or a subjunctive evaluation according to the matrix clause.

lessons.title: Event boundary and viewpoint
lessons.outcome: I can choose a past form to foreground an event or its background.

objectives.label: Use passato prossimo for a bounded event and imperfetto for the ongoing background in this context.

lessons.title: Degrees of inference
lessons.outcome: I can express strong or tentative inference about an earlier action.

objectives.label: Distinguish deve aver + participle from potrebbe aver + participle.

units.title: Advanced hypotheticals
units.description: Track unreal pasts, present results and implicit conditions.

lessons.title: Unreal past conditions
lessons.outcome: I can state an unreal past condition and its unreal result.

objectives.label: Use se + trapassato congiuntivo with a past conditional result.

lessons.title: Past cause, present result
lessons.outcome: I can connect an unreal past condition to a present state.

objectives.label: Use a past subjunctive condition with a present conditional result when the result is now.

lessons.title: Conditions without se
lessons.outcome: I can recognize an implied condition in a compact phrase.

objectives.label: Read senza + noun or con + noun as an implicit hypothetical when paired with a conditional.

units.title: Scope and unambiguous reference
units.description: Edit sentences so readers know exactly who and how many.

lessons.title: Resolve competing antecedents
lessons.outcome: I can remove a pronoun ambiguity in a short text.

objectives.label: Repeat a name or role when two referents could fit a pronoun.

lessons.title: Possession in relative clauses
lessons.outcome: I can express whose item is involved without a vague pronoun.

objectives.label: Use il cui / la cui + possessed noun with agreement to the possessed noun.

lessons.title: Quantifier scope under negation
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish “not all” from “none.”

objectives.label: Use non tutti for a partial negative and nessuno for a total negative.

units.title: Ellipsis and implication
units.description: Recover what a short expression leaves unsaid.

lessons.title: Parallel ellipsis
lessons.outcome: I can omit a repeated verb without hiding the relationship.

objectives.label: In balanced clauses, omit a recoverable repeated verb and keep the two parts parallel.

lessons.title: Implications of aspect verbs
lessons.outcome: I can infer what smettere and riprendere imply.

objectives.label: Recognize the earlier activity implied by smettere and riprendere.

units.title: Literary and historical forms
units.description: Read marked written forms and restate them in current usage.

lessons.title: Narrative past and present relevance
lessons.outcome: I can recognize the narrative function of passato remoto.

objectives.label: Use passato remoto for a closed historical narrative when the task asks for that style.

lessons.title: Marked order in literary narration
lessons.outcome: I can interpret a literary subject placed after the verb.

objectives.label: Recognize verb–subject order as a way of introducing a new actor in a narrative scene.

units.title: Variation and register
units.description: Recognize spoken constructions and choose edited alternatives.

lessons.title: Spoken dislocation in context
lessons.outcome: I can identify a spoken topic structure and recast it for a formal text.

objectives.label: Recognize clitic resumption as common in conversation; choose a neutral order for formal editing when needed.

lessons.title: Match request to audience
lessons.outcome: I can rewrite a direct request for a formal recipient while preserving the request.

objectives.label: Use a courteous conditional and a clear request complement in formal correspondence.

units.title: Edit a complex text
units.description: Correct logical links, compress repetition and keep parallel structures.

lessons.title: Repair a false logical link
lessons.outcome: I can replace a connector that misstates the relation between claims.

objectives.label: Choose a connector from the actual logic, not from surface punctuation.

lessons.title: Compress without hiding an agent
lessons.outcome: I can condense a clause while keeping who did what clear.

objectives.label: Use nominalization with a named agent when it is needed for meaning.

lessons.title: Parallel clauses in edited prose
lessons.outcome: I can repair an uneven pair of coordinated complements.

objectives.label: Give coordinated items the same grammatical form when they play the same role.

units.title: Interpret and produce
units.description: Apply grammar choices across short authentic-style situations.

lessons.title: Read stance across two sentences
lessons.outcome: I can identify what is asserted and what remains a possibility.

objectives.label: Track both source marking and grammatical mood across a short report.

lessons.title: Choose a precise final wording
lessons.outcome: I can produce a concise, logically precise sentence for a specified audience.

objectives.label: Combine condition, consequence and register in a single short rewrite.
